advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `closure_gaps` count actual un-enumerated gap paths (e.g. len(gaps)) separate from summary/orphan evidence lines.
evidence: Line 457-460 appends a summary line when len(gaps) > _MAX_REPORTED
`issues.extend(_orphaned_tests(...))` at line 461 adds orphan-test lines
`cov["closure_gaps"] = len(issues)` at line 462 then counts all of those as 'gaps'
advisory.finding: `closure_gaps` coverage is set to len(issues) after orphaned-test lines and the optional "N more un-enumerated path(s)" summary line are appended, so it conflates distinct gap paths with summary/orphan evidence lines rather than counting un-enumerated paths.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Count a required-empty grep AC whose command is present but not recognized as a sweep (grep-verb matched, argv None/no patterns) in closure_abstained so a non-recognized sweep is not silently invisible.
evidence: _grep_argv returns None for non-recursive grep: `return tokens[1:] if recursive else None` (line 177)
In _sweeps, a None sweep is skipped with no abstain increment: `if sweep is not None: sweeps.append(sweep)` (line 275-276); abstained only increments on re.error (line 272-273)
Litmus: 'checked and clean' (no required-empty greps) is indistinguishable from 'a required-empty grep AC was present but its command form was not recognized as a sweep'
advisory.finding: A non-recursive `grep foo file.py` AC under a required-empty line yields no sweep (grep without -r/-R returns None from _grep_argv) AND increments no abstain counter, so an intended-but-unrecognized sweep is silently invisible rather than counted.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound the number of sweeps (or short-circuit the tree walk) so a plan with many removal/grep ACs cannot force an O(files * sweeps) full-tree content scan.
evidence: _MAX_FILES = 50_000 (line 34)
_sweeps appends one sweep per required-empty grep span and one per removed symbol with no cap (lines 266-278)
_sweep_tree loops over all files and, for each, runs every scoped sweep regex: `for sweep in scoped: m = sweep.regex.search(text)` (lines 345-346)
Per-file per-sweep scan: `for sweep in scoped: m = sweep.regex.search(text)` over up to 1 MiB text (det_closure.py:345-346)
_covered is O(enumerated) per file: `return any(path == e or path.startswith(...) for e in enumerated)` (det_closure.py:101-102), called once per file in `_sweep_tree` (det_closure.py:339)
Tree size bounded only by `_MAX_FILES = 50_000`
advisory.finding: The number of sweeps is unbounded: each required-empty grep AC and each removed backticked identifier adds a _Sweep, and _sweep_tree runs every scoped sweep's regex over the contents of up to _MAX_FILES (50,000) files, reading each file's bytes.
merged_from: _sweep_tree scans each un-enumerated file's full text (up to 1 MiB) once per scoped sweep and calls _covered() (O(enumerated)) per file, giving cost proportional to files * (enumerated + sweeps * filesize). Driven by repository size rather than plan size, this grows super-linearly in the number of files × sweeps × enumerated paths.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add table-driven tests driving _grep_sweep via p6_ac_quality for -F, -w, -i, -E/egrep, and rg grep commands, asserting the resulting gap set.
evidence: det_closure.py:241-252 branch on `fixed = "F" in args.flags`, `basic = tokens[0] != "rg" ...`, `-w`/`--word-regexp`, and `-i`/`--ignore-case`
Concrete untested inputs: an AC item `` `rg -w fidelity_spot_eval` returns no hits`` (rg verb + word-regexp), or `` `grep -rF fidelity_spot_eval -- src` is empty`` (fixed-strings via recursive grep)
Every grep test in test_det_closure.py uses `git grep -n '...'` (lines 66, 97, 126, 138, 172, 182); none sets -F, -w, -i, -E, or uses rg/grep -r — ABSENCE rationale
advisory.finding: The grep-flag translation matrix is untested: no test exercises -F/--fixed-strings (re.escape path), -w/--word-regexp (word-boundary wrapping), -i/--ignore-case (IGNORECASE flag), -E/egrep ERE mode, or the `rg` verb. Only the git-grep BRE path (with `\|`/`\b`) is driven, so a regression in any other branch of _grep_sweep/_translate_pattern would go undetected.
scenarios: A refactor to _translate_pattern or the flag parsing silently breaks fixed-string or word-boundary matching while all tests stay green

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with >10 un-enumerated hit paths asserting exactly 10 path lines plus the 'N more un-enumerated path(s) match' summary.
evidence: det_closure.py:455-460: `list(gaps.items())[:_MAX_REPORTED]` and `if len(gaps) > _MAX_REPORTED: issues.append(f"... {len(gaps) - _MAX_REPORTED} more ...")`
Concrete violating input: a tree with 12 un-enumerated files each containing `fidelity_spot_eval` under a required-empty grep — the lint should report 10 plus a '2 more' line
search of test_det_closure.py for 'more un-enumerated' returns no matches — ABSENCE rationale
advisory.finding: The _MAX_REPORTED (10) truncation branch is untested: no test produces more than 10 un-enumerated gaps, so the summary line 'N more un-enumerated path(s) match' and the cap on the issues list are never exercised.
scenarios: An off-by-one in the slice or the overflow count regresses with no failing test

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] In test_grep_command_is_parsed_never_executed, add a liveness assertion (e.g. result.coverage['closure_sources'] >= 1) before asserting the marker is absent.
evidence: test_det_closure.py:140-141: `_p6(root, plan, file_impact=[...])` then only `assert not marker.exists()`

The producer-liveness anchor (e.g. asserting closure_sources >= 1, i.e. the command WAS parsed into a sweep) is absent, so a parse that silently yields zero sweeps also satisfies the absence assertion
advisory.finding: test_grep_command_is_parsed_never_executed is an absence-only oracle: it asserts `not marker.exists()` with no liveness check that the lint actually parsed/processed the grep command, so it would also pass if the command were silently never recognized (the whole sweep no-op).
scenarios: A change that makes `git grep ...; touch ...` fail to be recognized as a sweep at all would still leave the marker absent and keep this test green
advisory.suggested_fix: Capture the result and assert `result.coverage["closure_sources"] >= 1` alongside `assert not marker.exists()`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Read each tree file once (shared text cache / single pass) across _sweep_tree and _orphaned_tests instead of re-reading files in two separate full passes over `files`.
evidence: _sweep_tree reads files: `text = _read_text(root, rel) if scoped else None` (det_closure.py:342)
_orphaned_tests independently re-reads: `text = _read_text(root, rel)` inside a second `for rel in files:` loop (det_closure.py:413-416)
closure_issues calls both over the same `files` list: `gaps = _sweep_tree(...)` then `issues.extend(_orphaned_tests(ctx.repo_root, files, ctx.plan_text))` (det_closure.py:451, 461)
Cap attests real scale: `_MAX_FILES = 50_000` and `_MAX_FILE_BYTES = 1 << 20` (det_closure.py)
advisory.finding: det_closure walks the full repo file list and re-reads file contents TWICE per review — once in _sweep_tree and again in _orphaned_tests — with no shared text cache between the two passes, so a test file surviving both passes is read from disk twice. I/O cost grows linearly with repository size (up to _MAX_FILES=50_000 files), doubling the disk-read work on a path run on every plan review.
scenarios: A large repo (tens of thousands of tracked files) reviewed with a plan that both sweeps for symbols and deletes a module, triggering both _sweep_tree and _orphaned_tests full passes.
